incidents.vector: A cyberattack overnight targeted AFP Forum, the platform media clients use to browse and download AFP's stories, photos, and videos.
incidents.impact: AFP took its Forum platform offline as a precaution, disrupting global news content distribution to subscribers; no timeline given for restoration.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the Air Force's Cloud One cloud infrastructure platform, discovered during a platform upgrade within the past month.
incidents.impact: Potentially exposed large amounts of sensitive tactical and personnel data; it remains unclear who is responsible or whether data was accessed.

incidents.victim: UK Department for Work and Pensions
incidents.vector: A cyber incident of undisclosed nature prompted the department to take some online services offline as a precaution.
incidents.impact: Online services supporting benefits and pensions for millions were disrupted; regular payments were not affected. NCSC is assisting the investigation.

incidents.vector: Hackers obtained employee authentication tokens to access SAP's GitHub-hosted software development environment and copy/modify source code.
incidents.impact: Potential unauthorized access to proprietary source code; SAP says no evidence yet of customer business data access. GitHub access was restricted and signing keys replaced.

incidents.vector: An attacker compromised an employee's GitHub account and used it to push malicious code to 1Password's backend systems.
incidents.impact: Customer names and email addresses were stolen; the company says password vaults remained unaffected and secure.

incidents.vector: A phishing email opened in October gave attackers access to the ministry's visa-issuing system.
incidents.impact: Visa and passport issuance systems were compromised; officials believe a criminal group is using the access to sell visas and fake identities. The system remains running to avoid stranding travelers.

incidents.vector: An attacker used valid credentials to access Todoist's production systems.
incidents.impact: Email addresses and password hashes were stolen for about 6% of Todoist's users.

incidents.vector: Details of the intrusion method have not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: The Australian energy provider halted trading of its stock on the ASX as a precaution following the breach.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the Rackspace Spot cloud marketplace platform and stole customer account credentials.
incidents.impact: Customer credentials were stolen; Rackspace is winding down the Spot service entirely, with full retirement set for December 8.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed FIFA's systems and exfiltrated personal and business information.
incidents.impact: A new extortion group calling itself the 'Handsome Boy Hacking Club' claimed credit and leaked data from FIFA on its dark web site.

incidents.victim: Cyprus airline, telecom, and critical infrastructure organizations
incidents.vector: A newly identified group ("Volant Manticore") uses fake AI-generated resume phishing lures to deliver a custom backdoor that communicates over the decentralized IPFS network.
incidents.impact: Intelligence-gathering campaign against a Cypriot airline, telecom providers, critical infrastructure, and a suspected government/military entity; activity has since expanded to Saudi Arabia.

incidents.vector: An unauthorized party gained access to a limited subset of FinCEN's systems.
incidents.impact: The BSA E-Filing portal and related services were partially taken offline; filing deadlines were extended. No evidence of a breach of beneficial ownership databases to date.

incidents.victim: Japan Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached the ministry's government procurement system, detected on October 1 and disclosed nearly two months later.
incidents.impact: Potentially exposed about 1,700 email addresses and 164,000 business records tied to companies eligible for government tenders; no evidence of public disclosure or misuse found so far.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack in September; the Qilin ransomware group claimed responsibility.
incidents.impact: May have compromised the personal information of more than 11 million customers, business partners, employees, and job applicants of the Japanese railway operator.

incidents.victim: CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence
incidents.vector: Hackers breached an unclassified open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system used by both agencies.
incidents.impact: Exposed unclassified data that could reveal what analysts were searching for and which topics they were tracking; classified networks were not affected.

incidents.vector: A threat actor exploited a secrets-leaking flaw in Microsoft Azure API Management Classic to steal API credentials.
incidents.impact: Norwegian energy providers' systems were accessed using the stolen credentials; Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) issued an advisory and Microsoft has deployed updates, though not all instances may be patched.

incidents.vector: Attackers stole data from a shared IT provider serving Flemish municipal governments.
incidents.impact: Personal data of 1.2 million Flemish citizens was stolen, with some already being sold online.

incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a zero-day untrusted-deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-129514) to take over six backend servers.
incidents.impact: No unauthorized package modifications were found, but user data exposure could not be ruled out since database reads weren't logged; all backend credentials were rotated.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote-access service.
incidents.impact: Backdoors disguised as a cron process were installed on customer travel routers and IP KVM devices; GL.iNet blocked the attack path and released firmware fixes.

incidents.victim: VMware vCenter / BeyondTrust Remote Support customer
incidents.vector: PRC-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE exploited zero-days in BeyondTrust Remote Support and VMware vCenter (CVE-2026-123890) to create an administrator session and deploy custom malware.
incidents.impact: Full compromise of the vCenter environment, including credential theft, database exfiltration, and creation of a backdoor SSO administrator account.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency, gaming, and VoIP software users (Europe)
incidents.vector: Trojanized installers and lure files (fake PDFs, messaging app installers) deliver the Overlord RAT and a Python-based infostealer, using Solana blockchain transactions for resilient command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Credential and cryptocurrency theft from targeted individuals across Europe, with activity suspected of ties to North Korean actors.

incidents.victim: 178+ organizations including HSBC, BBC, CNN, Equifax, and Zoom
incidents.vector: An attacker exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject Magecart-style malicious JavaScript into customer projects, served from Optimizely's legitimate CDN.
incidents.impact: Payment card and cryptocurrency theft from site visitors, plus mobile exploit kits delivered to outdated iPhones/iPads; roughly $7,500 in cryptocurrency confirmed stolen before remediation.

incidents.victim: U.S. hospitals, healthcare entities, and schools (multiple states)
incidents.vector: Conspiracy affiliated with INC and Lynx ransomware gained network access, exfiltrated data, and extorted victims by threatening to release stolen records.
incidents.impact: Over 50 terabytes of data, including more than 70 million confidential health records, were stolen, generating over $500 million in ransom demands; a key member was extradited from Italy to face charges.

incidents.vector: North Korean cyber actors stole more than $6 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance.
incidents.impact: The Justice Department has filed to forfeit over $1.1 billion in recovered stablecoin proceeds, part of roughly $2.9 billion recovered to date from the theft.
